plain_text:
Published November 25, 2026, 12:48 p.m.
Meeting will take place at Holyoke City Hall, 536 Dwight St
and can also be accessed remotely via www.zoom.us
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/85914960000?pwd=QVBqSkJvd0pSZENmNFdDbnVXTnVTUT09
Meeting ID: 859 1496 0000 Meeting Passcode: 657908 or by call in at 1 (646) 558-8656 with
same Meeting ID and Passcode.
Live Spanish interpretation will be available on local access channel 15 using the television's
SAP option, through the live stream on the city website, as well as on the Zoom feed by clicking
the interpretation option and choosing Spanish.
Tuesday, December 1, 2026
6:30 PM
AGENDA
PRESIDENT'S REPORT
PUBLIC HEARING
PUBLIC COMMENT
REGULAR AND PENDING EXECUTIVE SESSION MINUTES
1. June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 Executive Session Minutes -
Reviewed and ready for partial release as of September 17, 2025
2. June 11, 2024, September 4, 2024, and April 15, 2025 Executive Session Minutes -
Reviewed and ready for partial release as of September 17, 2025
3. From City Clerk Brenna Murphy Leary and Admin. Assistant Jeffery
Anderson-Burgos-meeting minutes from November 17, 2026 meeting
LAID ON THE TABLE
4. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order that Section 6.4.6 Signs in
Business and Industrial Districts, Size Limitations Table, of the Zoning Ordinance be amended
to increase the maximum surface area permitted for each sign by special permit from 80 sf to
400 sf by special permit of the Planning Board, for projects having 50,000 sf of building area or
greater, or for projects of such similar size and scale that said increased sign size is
appropriate. In crafting this special permit, the Council might wish to consider the value of
specifying findings and conditions beyond those already specified in Section 9.3 of the Zoning
Ordinance that may be necessary to ensure that proposed signs have no undue impact on
abutting neighborhoods or residences.
Recommended that the order be adopted.
COMMUNICATIONS
5. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-letter appointing Mr. Jason Roriguez to serve on the
Commission on Disabilities. Mr. Rodriguez will replace Ms. Lyn Horan and will serve the
remainder of her term; said term will expire on March 1, 2028.
6. From Mayor Joshua Garcia-Holyoke Capital Improvement Plan Final FY26-FY30
7. From CAFO Tj Plante-Council Memo Capital Improvement Plan FY26-FY30
8. From CAFO Tj Plante-Council Bond Authorization Memo 11.23.26
9. From City Solicitor Lisa Ball- Settlement Agreement Between the City of Holyoke and the
IBPC Local #388
10. From City Solicitor Lisa Ball - Settlement Agreement Between the City of Holyoke and the
IBPC Local #409.pdf
11. From City Solicitor Lisa Ball- Red-lined contract: Local 409 Police Supervisors
7/1/25-6/30/26
12. From City Solicitor Lisa Ball- Red-lined contract: Local 409 Police Supervisors
7/1/26-6/30/29
13. From Human Resource Director Kelly Curran-Agreement between the City of Holyoke and
the IBPC #388 25-26
14. From Human Resource Director Kelly Curran-Agreement between the City of Holyoke and
the IBPC #388 26-29
15. From Danie Glanville, Assistant City Solictor-legal opion for Councilor Vacon regarding the
Planning Board
16. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 Sewer Enterprise Expense YTD
Report-Totals
17. From City Comptroller Sharon Bittner-Willis, FY2027 General Fund Expense YTD
Report-Totals
18. From Cheryl Allen, Director of Internal Audit - Internal Audit Charter
19. From Cheryl Allen, Director of Internal Audit- Finance Committee Audit Committee
Structure
20. From Holyoke Water Commission-communication regarding Wyckoff Country Club
21. From Board of Fire Commissioners-meeting minutes from October 21, 2026
PETITIONS
REPORTS OF COMMITTEES
22. The Committee on Ordinance to whom was referred an order That the DPW move the
current Handicap parking space that is located near 420 Dwight Street and move it in front of
420 Dwight Street.
The distance that this handicap parking spot is from a Holyoke business (THE PLAN) severely
limits the ability of handicap people to get to the ramp located at THE PLAN which is slightly
above 420 Dwight Street.
Awaiting disposition
23. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that in accordance with M.G.L.
Chapter 44 Sec. 53A, the City Council hereby accepts the provisions of the "FY27 EXECUTIVE
OFFICE OF ENERGY & ENVIRONMENTAL AFFAIRS (EEA) DAM AND SEAWALL
PROGRAM, $1,000,000.00, $182,175.00 CASH MATCH/$6,900.00 IN KIND MATCH" grant,
and authorizes the establishment of a Fund or other method appropriate for the accounting of
the receipts and expenditures of all resources associated with the administration of said grant.
Sec 2-509 - Grant Reporting
Any city department, of which has received grant funding by approval of the city council
pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws, or any other authorizing criteria, shall within a
reasonable period of time, but no later than 60 days from the conclusion of said grant, generate
a detailed report which outlines the planned outcomes with the documented actual results. Said
report shall be submitted to the city clerk for addition to the city council's next agenda.
Recommended that the order be adopted.
24. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred an order that the amount of eighteen
million and two hundred twenty-five thousand dollars ($18,225,000) is appropriated for the
purpose of financing the demolition, remodeling, reconstruction, engineering, construction,
equipping or re-equipping of various city facilities, roads, and sidewalks, including the payment
of costs incidental or related thereto, as set forth in Exhibit A hereto. To meet this appropriation
the Treasurer, with the approval of the Mayor is authorized to borrow said amount under and
pursuant to M.G.L. Chapter 44, Section 7 or any other enabling authority.
FURTHER ORDERED: That the Mayor is authorized to contract for and expend any state aid
available for the project; and that the Mayor is authorized to take any other action necessary or
convenient to carry out these projects.
FURTHER ORDERED: That the Treasurer is authorized to file an application to qualify under
Chapter 44A of the General Laws any and all of the bonds or notes authorized to be issued
pursuant to this Order, and to provide such information and execute such documents as may
be required for such purposes.
FURTHER ORDERED: That there shall be no change in the purpose of this bond authorization
without prior vote of approval by the Holyoke City Council.
Recommended that the order be adopted.
25. The Committee on Finance to whom was referred a communication From Timothy J Plante,
Chief Administration and Finance Officer, Financial Departments Organizational Chart
Recommended that the communication be referred to the Ordinance Committee.
26. The Committee on Public Service to whom was referred a communication From Mayor
Joshua Garcia-letter appointing Ms. Amelia Mosley of 140 Lincoln St. to serve on the new
Historical Commission Term will expire May 1, 2027.
Recommended that the appointment be confirmed.
27. The Committee on Public Service to whom was referred a communication From Mayor
Joshua Garcia- letter appointing Dr. Rebecca Lisi of 25 Reservation Rd. to serve a full 5 year
term to the Holyoke Redevelopment Authority, expiring November 1, 2031.
Recommended that the appointment be confirmed.
28. The Committee on Public Service to whom was referred a communication from Mayor
Joshua Garcia, letter appointing several members to serve on the Recycling Advisory
Committee. Members will serve a three-year term expiring August 2026.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
29. The Committee on Public Service to whom was referred an order that the City Council adpt
the attached resolution regarding Increased Transparency in Board Communication with
Citizens.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
30. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that Council Rule 8D
be struck in its entirety, that Rule 8F be amended to read, "In all cases the President shall have
the privilege of discussing all matters before the Council and of voting thereon.," and that Rule
8 be renumbered accordingly. The revised rule would serve the public's interest in their elected
Councilor being able to participate fully in the Council's decisions, and is consistent with the
practice of the Council's committees and with the rules of other city boards and commissions.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
31. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order that the Council
Rules be examined and revised as necessary to clarify the Rule 9 provisions relating to legal
form and committee procedure.
Recommended that the order be adopted.
32. The Committee on Charter and Rules to whom was referred an order Add to rule 9h: when
an order has been deemed tabled after the chair has not taken it up for 45 business days, upon
request of the maker, the chair shall place the order on the next agenda to ensure compliance
with the open meeting law.
Recommended that the order be adopted.
MOTIONS, ORDERS AND RESOLUTIONS
33. Magrath-Smith - Ordered, that the Ordinance Committee consider the impacts of the recent
vote by state cannabis regulators to allow drive-through operations at existing cannabis
facilities, and any ordinance changes needed or desired as a result.
34. Murphy-Romboletti - ORDERED:That the classification for the Director of Assessing is
hereby amended by reclassifying the position of Director of Assessing from Grade 9 to Grade
13 on the Schedule A Pay Schedule.
35. Panitch, Magrath-Smith: Ordered: in order to ensure consistency for applicants, and to
ensure compliance with the requirements set forth in our ordinances and in applicable
provisions of state law, that the Council develop and adopt a template to use in granting or
denying special permits for cannabis uses. Receive and send to Charter and Rules.
36. Vacon- ORDER: that we amend our finance ordinance 2-137 & other sections as necessary
by adding/amending the language for the Director of Internal Audit: see draft below:
D. When a vacancy of the Director of Internal Audit occurs, the HR Department shall post the
position including the required qualifications and submit all applications to the city council. The
Public Service Committee of the city council shall review applications, interview qualified
applicants & recommend to the city council the names of not less than two candidates whom it
believes to be best suited to perform the duties of the Auditor. If the Public Service committee
determines that there are not at least two candidates qualified to perform the duties of the
Director of Internal Audit, the Public Service Committee shall report to the city council that it is
unable to complete its assigned task. In that event, the city council shall reopen the search and
the HR Department shall repost the position. While filling the vacancy of an auditor the
Comptroller will temporarily assume the duties of the Director of Internal Audit.
The Comptroller shall serve ex-officio on the Retirement Board & the HealthTrust
The audit committee will be the (?)Public Service Committee of the city council. The committee
needs to be determined.
Reporting:
Audit plans, charters, and major findings are reported to the city council
Day-to-day operations, HR, and logistics are reported to the CAFO
37. Vacon- ORDER: That a copy of the Clifton & Larson contract & the contract with Rory
Casey be provided to the City Council. Send to Finance & CAFO.
38. Devine-Ordered, that in accordance with M.G.L. Chapter 44 Sec. 53A, the City Council
hereby accepts the provisions of the "FY27 MUNICIPAL AND TRIBAL TECHNICAL
ASSISTANCE (MTTA), $75,000.00, NO MATCH" grant, and authorizes the establishment of a
Fund or other method appropriate for the accounting of the receipts and expenditures of all
resources associated with the administration of said grant.
Sec 2-509 - Grant Reporting
Any city department, of which has received grant funding by approval of the city council
pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws, or any other authorizing criteria, shall within a
reasonable period of time, but no later than 60 days from the conclusion of said grant, generate
a detailed report which outlines the planned outcomes with the documented actual results. Said
report shall be submitted to the city clerk for addition to the city council's next agenda.
39. Devine- Since most if not all grants are sent to the Finance Committee, any City
department, which has applied and received a grant that is approved by the City Council
persuant to Massachusetts General Laws or other authorizing criteria, shall be reminded that
the grant applicant shall within a reasonable time frame once the grant is completed shall send
a copy of the final results to the City Council to be placed on the City Council Agenda under
"Communications".
40. Devine-Ordered, that the City Council consider for its approval the FY27 budget from the
Holyoke Community Preservation Committee.
41. Devine-That the amount of two million dollars ($2,000,000) is appropriated for the purpose
of financing the purchase and equipping of vehicles, including the payment of costs incidental
or related thereto, as set forth in Exhibit A hereto. To meet this appropriation, the Treasurer,
with the approval of the Mayor is authorized to borrow said amount under and pursuant to
M.G.L. Chapter 44, Section 7 or any other enabling authority.
FURTHER ORDERED: That the Mayor is authorized to contract for and expend any state aid
available for the project; and that the Mayor is authorized to take any other action necessary or
convenient to carry out these projects.
FURTHER ORDERED: That the Treasurer is authorized to file an application to qualify under
Chapter 44A of the General Laws any and all of the bonds or notes authorized to be issued
pursuant to this
Order, and to provide such information and execute such documents as may be required for
such purposes.
FURTHER ORDERED: That there shall be no change in the purpose of this bond authorization
without prior vote of approval by the Holyoke City Council.
42. DEVINE - Ordered, that in accordance with M.G.L. Chapter 44 Sec. 64, that the amount of
FOUR HUNDRED TWENTY-FIVE AND 00/100 DOLLARS ($425.00) be authorized from the
MAYOR Department's DUES AND SUBSCRIPTIONS (11212-57300) appropriation in fiscal
year 2027 for goods/services received in fiscal year 2026 which were unencumbered at the
2026 fiscal year end.
43. Greaney - Ordered that Senior Center staff ensure that handicapped accessible tables at
the Holyoke Senior Center café meet federal ADA regulations as well as state accessibility
codes under Mass Architectural Board 521 CMR 12.
Addendum:
LATE FILES FROM PREVIOUS MEETING
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order Invite the Tree Warden and
Director of Conservation to attend an upcoming Public Safety meeting to present a plan for
addressing vacant tree pits, stumps, hazardous trees, and other outstanding tree related needs
throughout the City.
Recommended that the order has been complied with.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that the HPD, HFD & DPW
provide a quarterly summary (no individual information) report to the city council on employee
injuries including; number of employees out injured, length of time out, & nature of injuries &
any actions taken to reduce injuries, along with any other information the department wishes to
include.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that a monthly standing order
be added to Public Safety meetings where the committee reviews the See-Click-Fix Report and
the status of logged issues.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that a plan be presented to
Public Safety concerning how See-Click-Fix can be effectively implemented through DPW,
Engineering, and Council, including how it can be made prominent on the city website, how
councilors can log issues from constituents, what communication structure can be used to
respond to people who log issues, and how a public-facing report can be shared online
showing the status of issues that were logged. Consider also if a "Driving Speed/Traffic
Complaint" category can be added.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order The condition of the sidewalk
on Northampton St between West Glen and Clark Streets is virtually impassable especially for
persons with disabilities.
Recommended that the order has been complied with.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order The City Engineer and/or
VEOLIA suggest improvements to the sidewalk and catch basin near 5 Martin St. (at the corner
of Westfield Rd and Martin). Owner's contractor noted the sidewalk is too high and the design
causes water to pool on parking lot; the catch basin is above-grade is not catching storm water.
Owner very willing to confer with City Engineer on this matter.
Recommended that the order has been complied with.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order The DPW install a protective
wraparound barrier (lattice, wire) the Holyoke Railroad platform. Unfortunately people are using
this for protection from the elements but it is a very dangerous location and I don't want anyone
to stumble onto the rail tracks as recently happened in Northampton.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that the City Engineer review
Old Jarvis Ave to address traffic safety concerns of several residents, including vehicles
traveling at high speeds and large trucks traveling on the street on a regular basis. Residents
are asking for consideration of a truck exclusion, making it a one way, and/or barriers at one
end making it a dead end. Residents have expressed that speed humps were installed 15
years ago, but they did not prevent speeding.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order DPW & engineer evaluate the
conditions at Homestead & Mayer & make recommendations for needed infrastructure
improvements and provide a cost estimate. Flooding has been occurring there for years and
has worsened with recent storms, causing a safety hazard.
Recommended that the order has been complied with.
The Committee on Public Safety to whom was referred an order that a sign indicating no truck
outlet be placed at the end of Rhode Island St (similar to McGrady & Franks). Tractor Trailer
drivers are damaging the road/utilities when entering the area by mistake.
Recommended that the order be given a leave to withdraw.
Per City Council rule 2B, meeting shall end by 10 PM unless an extension is approved by a
two-thirds majority of those present. If any items remain, those items will be added to the
beginning of the next regular meeting.
The listing of matters are those reasonably anticipated by the chair which may be
discussed at the meeting.
Not all items listed may in fact be discussed and other items not listed may also be
brought up for discussion to the extent permitted by law
